findings.body: `0008` depends on `billing.0007_add_reason`, and this PR deletes that file. Django’s migration loader will raise `NodeNotFoundError` on `migrate` / `showmigrations` because the parent node is gone. summary:
I would not merge until the migration graph is restored: `0008_drop_reason` depends on `billing.0007_add_reason`, which this PR deletes.

Django will raise `NodeNotFoundError` on `migrate` / `showmigrations` because the parent node is missing from disk. The working drop-column path is to keep `0007_add_reason.py` and let `0008` run `RemoveField`. Databases that already applied 0007 also need that file so `django_migrations` still matches the tree.

I could not verify application usage of `void_reason` — this workspace only contains the two migration files — so I treated the unused-column claim as given. `RemoveField` will still DROP the column and discard any stored values.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
